projects.name: Chorus
projects.summary: Pools RAM and VRAM across machines on a LAN to run one large model.

body.p: Most machines can't fit a large model on their own. Chorus lets several Windows machines on the same network share the load, so the model runs across the pool instead of on one box. Each node contributes the memory and compute it can spare; the app handles discovery, distribution, and keeping the nodes in step.

The hard part isn't inference — it's coordination. Nodes join and leave, links are slower than local memory, and the whole thing has to degrade instead of failing. The UI is a Tauri shell over a React front end, with the scheduling and networking in Rust.

projects.name: Ai Imam
projects.summary: Islamic AI assistant — Android client over a Python backend.

body.p: An assistant for Islamic questions and daily practice, packaged as a native Android app. The app is a thin, fast client; the reasoning and retrieval live in a Python backend that can be updated without shipping a new build.

Splitting the app from the model means the answers can improve weekly while the install stays stable. The work was mostly in keeping the two in sync and making the app feel instant while the backend thinks.

projects.name: LoadShedding Alert
projects.summary: Local-first power-cut pre-alerts, built for Bangladesh.

body.p: Warns people before the power goes, not after. A FastAPI backend keeps the schedules and pushes alerts to subscribers, with the whole stack containerised so it can run on cheap hardware.

The data is messy and changes constantly, and the network is exactly what you don't have when the power cuts. Design decisions leaned local-first: cache what you can, alert early, and don't block on a perfect connection.

projects.name: Automated Chatbot
projects.summary: Custom AI chatbot answering on Messenger and WhatsApp.

body.p: A single bot that answers on both Messenger and WhatsApp, with an admin channel for commands and adjustments. Runs on a small always-on machine rather than paying for hosting.
Two messaging platforms, two very different sets of rules about what you can send and how fast. The interesting work is the conversation state and the queueing, not the model.

projects.name: My Masjid Azan
projects.summary: Prayer times with a home-screen widget that resizes to any size.

body.p: Shows the next prayer and the day's times, with a widget that fits whatever space the home screen gives it — from a single line to a full block.

Android widgets resize continuously and the system gives you very little to work with. Getting the layout smooth at every size meant treating the widget as a small layout engine rather than a fixed view.

projects.name: PC Controller
projects.summary: Drive a desktop from a phone — Python server, Android client.

body.p: A small server on the PC and an app on the phone: volume, media, shutdown, and the everyday controls you'd otherwise walk across the room for. Both packaged as standalone builds — an .exe and an .apk.
Pairing has to work without configuration on a network you don't control. Discovery, reconnect, and a UI that stays usable when the link drops were most of the work.

projects.name: YouTube FastForward
projects.summary: Playback speed plus measurement-driven volume levelling.

body.p: Keyboard-driven playback speed, and a leveller that reads the actual loudness of the audio and normalises it, so quiet videos and loud ads end up at the same volume.

Volume levelling by measurement rather than guesswork: a rolling dBFS reading feeds an automatic gain control. Most of the bug history came from edge cases — the first Short, the stalled measurement window, the watchdog that killed the leveller after a track change.
Connects people who cook at home with people who want to eat it. Browsing, ordering, and the usual marketplace flow, built as a native Android app.
Started as a web build, later rebuilt natively for the feel and the platform integration. Carrying the design language across that change without losing the details was the real exercise.

projects.name: Portable AI Assistant
projects.summary: Pocket assistant wired to a hosted LLM API.

body.p: An assistant that lives on the phone but does its thinking through a fast hosted model API, with a small Python layer for the parts that don't belong in the client.
Keeping latency low on mobile means streaming responses and never blocking the interface. Most of the tuning was in how much context gets sent and when.

projects.name: No Ads Qibla Compass
projects.summary: Qibla direction from GPS and sensors, no advertising.

body.p: Finds the direction of the Kaaba using position and the device's sensors, and points at it. No ads, no accounts, no tracking.
Compasses drift and phones lie about their sensors. The work was in calibration and in being honest when accuracy is poor instead of confidently pointing the wrong way.

projects.name: Calling Bell App
projects.summary: Two phones on one Wi-Fi act as doorbell and receiver.

body.p: One phone sits by the door, one lives with you. Press the bell and the receiver rings wherever it is on the network — no cloud, no subscription.
Local discovery between two devices with no server in the middle, and staying paired after both have been asleep.

projects.name: ShortLoop
projects.summary: Pipeline for producing short-form video, end to end.

body.p: Takes an idea or a source clip and carries it through to a finished short — script, cut, captions, upload — with as little manual handling as possible.
Automation that runs unattended has to survive interruptions and resume cleanly. Most of the design is state and recovery, not the creative step.

projects.name: WattScope
projects.summary: Power-supply wattage calculator for PC builds.

body.p: Add up the parts of a build and get an honest recommendation for how much power supply it needs, with headroom rather than a marketing number.
A small tool where the value is entirely in the numbers being right and the interface staying out of the way.

projects.name: Volume Control Pro
projects.summary: Fine-grained volume control the stock panel never gave you.

body.p: More steps, per-stream control, and the adjustments Android's default panel hides behind three taps.
Android's audio streams are separate and each has its own rules. Presenting them together without confusing anyone was the whole design problem.

projects.name: Neon Breaker
projects.summary: Offline brick breaker — one level, three lives, no install.

body.p: A DX Ball-style brick breaker in a single page. Open the file, the game runs — no server, no network, no downloaded assets.
Built to be one level that feels finished: fixed collision, readable feedback, and a difficulty curve that's tight rather than long.

projects.name: DX Ball Antigravity
projects.summary: DX Ball variant with dynamic ball-speed scaling.

body.p: A fast-completion take on DX Ball: one level, and the ball speeds up as the grid empties, so the last bricks are the hardest.
Scaling speed dynamically changes how the game feels more than any amount of level design. Tuning it so it stays fair is the whole trick.

projects.name: Flappy Bird
projects.summary: Clone in a single HTML file, open and play.

body.p: The classic, rebuilt as a single file. One tap, one obstacle pattern, one score that you keep trying to beat.
The game is small enough to hold in your head entirely, which makes it a good way to keep your hands on the fundamentals.
